brief.summary: Lichen is an in-process semantic search runtime compiled to WASM that runs inside the app in the browser, on the edge, on a device, or in the cloud, with no separate vector database service. A developer adds it through the TypeScript or Python SDK, indexes datasets via the Lichen Portal, and calls a local search function that returns results in under 10 ms for use inside a voice or copilot turn loop.

capabilities.statement: Run semantic search with <10 ms latency without a vector database
capabilities.painSolved: Every retrieval call in a voice turn pays a network round trip and vector DB query time, so the agent's reply latency blows past the budget before the LLM even starts; sub-10 ms in-process search removes the separate service from that path.

capabilities.statement: Run retrieval directly in the browser, on the edge, on a device, or in the cloud
capabilities.painSolved: Retrieval is locked to one server region, so browser or device features either proxy every query to the cloud or ship no search at all; the same search can run where the user is, on edge or device, without rewriting the pipeline.

capabilities.statement: Run semantic search in-process inside the app, compiled to WASM, so there is no network hop and it works offline
capabilities.painSolved: A hosted vector DB or local server must be reachable for every query, so the feature breaks on flaky mobile networks or offline and every lookup leaks data off the device; an in-process WASM index removes the hop and keeps the lookup local.

capabilities.statement: Use TypeScript and Python SDKs to add retrieval to an application
capabilities.painSolved: Wiring retrieval into a TypeScript web app or a Python agent service means hand-building HTTP clients, auth, and serialization around a database API; the SDKs give a direct search call in the language the app already uses.

capabilities.statement: Build and index datasets through the Lichen Portal, with file uploads and downloads on paid tiers
capabilities.painSolved: Building and refreshing an index means writing ingestion scripts and hosting a database to load them into; the portal takes dataset uploads and downloads so the index is produced without standing up infrastructure (file transfer on paid tiers).

capabilities.statement: Keep indexes up to date with a Continuous Sync Engine and manage unlimited projects and indexes (Hobbyist tier)
capabilities.painSolved: When source documents change, the developer writes cron jobs and reindex pipelines to keep the vector store current and stale results leak into answers; the Continuous Sync Engine keeps indexes updated automatically (Hobbyist tier).

capabilities.statement: Sub-10 ms retrieval for voice agents, copilots and multimodal apps
capabilities.painSolved: Voice agents, copilots, and multimodal apps need retrieval inside a conversational turn of a few hundred milliseconds total, but typical hosted retrieval consumes most of that budget; sub-10 ms retrieval leaves the turn budget for the model and speech stages.

capabilities.statement: Lichen Inference, a separate offering, is in private beta and available by request. Its exact function is not described in the provided sources.
capabilities.painSolved: Teams want an inference capability alongside retrieval, but the exact function is not described in the provided sources; the developer can only request private beta access and cannot yet plan around it.

vsCompetitors.name: Pinecone

vsCompetitors.ourEdge: Runs in-process in the browser, on edge, or on device with no network hop to a hosted index, which is the source of the sub-10 ms path; works offline.

vsCompetitors.name: Qdrant
vsCompetitors.theirCost: A vector database service that must be self-hosted or managed; every query goes to a separate server process that the team deploys, scales, and monitors.
vsCompetitors.ourEdge: No separate vector database service to deploy or query; retrieval is embedded in the app and can run offline.

vsCompetitors.name: Chroma
vsCompetitors.theirCost: Open-source embedding database typically run as a server for RAG prototypes; adds a service process and a query round trip when used beyond local prototyping.
vsCompetitors.ourEdge: Built for real-time voice-agent latency with WASM in-browser and edge execution and TypeScript and Python SDKs, instead of a server process.

vsCompetitors.name: LanceDB
vsCompetitors.theirCost: Embedded vector database that still requires its own storage and index management inside the app and is not positioned for browser WASM voice-turn latency.
vsCompetitors.ourEdge: Targets a sub-10 ms retrieval path that runs in the browser via WASM and offline, aimed at voice agents.

vsCompetitors.name: Hosted vector DB plus embedding API (DIY RAG stack)
vsCompetitors.theirCost: Each query chains an embedding API call and a vector DB query: multiple network hops, per-call pricing for both, glue code per app, and data leaves the device for every lookup.
vsCompetitors.ourEdge: Replaces the multi-hop embedding-plus-query stack with one in-process search, removing the network round trips.

mechanism.pain: Each retrieval call crosses a network to a hosted vector DB, consuming the few hundred ms turn budget before the LLM and speech stages run.

events.message: Segment: Obsidian-style local-first note-app plugin authors

mechanism.pain: Semantic note search needs a local Chroma server or hosted index, so notes leave the device or the feature fails offline on a laptop.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: Plugin authors assume a server is required, not realizing their users' vaults can be searched fully in-process on the desktop.

events.message: Segment: Browser extension authors building on-page semantic search

segment.name: Browser extension authors building on-page semantic search

mechanism.pain: Extensions proxy every page query to a hosted vector DB plus embedding API, adding round trips and sending browsing content to a third party.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: Extension builders rarely think of retrieval as a client-side library since they treat search as a backend service.

events.message: Segment: NPC dialogue retrieval teams in game engines

segment.name: NPC dialogue retrieval teams in game engines

mechanism.pain: NPC lore lookups call a hosted vector DB per player utterance, adding network latency that stalls in-game dialogue during a frame-sensitive interaction.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: Game studios treat lore as static data, not as a live retrieval problem needing sub-10 ms responses inside the engine.

events.message: Segment: Field robotics teams needing offline manual lookup on edge boards

segment.name: Field robotics teams needing offline manual lookup on edge boards

mechanism.pain: Robots in the field query a cloud Qdrant instance over unreliable links, so technicians lose manual lookup when connectivity drops.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: Robotics teams assume retrieval belongs in the cloud, overlooking on-board search on ARM hardware with no network.

events.message: Segment: Endpoint security agents doing on-device threat-intel similarity search

segment.name: Endpoint security agents doing on-device threat-intel similarity search

mechanism.pain: Endpoint agents send telemetry to a hosted vector DB for similarity matching, leaking device data and failing when the host is air-gapped.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: Security vendors centralize matching for updates, not expecting a local in-process index to be fast enough on endpoints.

events.message: Segment: Nightly re-indexing teams for 50M-document enterprise corpora

segment.name: Nightly re-indexing teams for 50M-document enterprise corpora

mechanism.pain: Teams rebuild a distributed Qdrant or Pinecone index nightly across sharded clusters; this in-process approach may lack the scale and sharding they need.
mechanism.whyNonObvious: It is a plausible fit for sync automation, but the incumbent's distributed sharding likely wins at this corpus size.

segments.name: Voice-agent teams needing fast retrieval inside live turns

mechanism.pain: Each retrieval call crosses a network to a hosted vector DB, consuming the few hundred ms turn budget before the LLM and speech stages run.

topObjections: Our service is Java 17 Spring Boot and the SDKs are TypeScript and Python only, and sending PHI-adjacent clinical policy docs to a vendor-hosted portal or in-process index would need a full security assessment we don't have time for.

Uploading formulary and interaction data to a new vendor's Portal triggers the hospital DPA process again, adding weeks, and our 15 ms local lookup gains nothing from sub-10 ms while cold start is unaddressed.

hooks.angle: Plugin authors keep rebuilding the same local stack (markdown-aware chunking, persistent vectors, mtime-gated incremental indexing) and the consent-gated embedding flow, just to keep note text on-device. An in-process index removes the separate server piece.

Depending on another plugin or process for semantic search is fragile: a slow Smart Connections start leaves search 'not ready' until reload. Embedding the index in the plugin's own process removes that startup race.

Devs want notes search that is offline and private (local model preference, 100% offline semantic search, no API key or cloud call), and are vibe-coding local vector search themselves. Offer a drop-in alternative to hand-rolled or server-based setups.

No obligation to post, no scripted praise, and honest criticism or bug reports are welcome. Lead with the offline/in-process problem the author already has, link their own issue or post where relevant, and keep every draft for a human to review, edit, and post manually.
